title: Identifying Non-Ideal Reaction-Diffusion Systems Unable to Maintain Diffusion Out-of-Equilibrium
authors: Francesco Avanzini, Timur Aslyamov, Massimiliano Esposito
abstract: We develop a general method, based on the construction of a kinetic potential acting as a Lyapunov function, to establish when diffusion necessarily equilibrates in non-ideal reaction-diffusion systems, under arbitrary driving by autonomous homogeneous chemostats. Using this method, we generalize the results of J. Chem. Phys. 161, 174108 (2024) by relaxing some of the underlying assumptions. Specifically, we show that diffusion equilibrates in reaction-diffusion systems whose chemical reaction network is either pseudo-detailed balanced, with reaction fluxes controlled by the stoichiometry of reactants and products, or complex balanced, with reaction fluxes controlled only by the stoichiometry of the reactants. The different constraints on the reaction fluxes are shown to originate from the distinct stoichiometric properties of the two classes of networks.
summary: This paper establishes a general theoretical method using a kinetic potential to determine when diffusion reaches equilibrium in complex reaction-diffusion systems. It proves that equilibration occurs if the system's underlying chemical network possesses specific topological properties (pseudo-detailed or complex balance) and satisfies associated flux constraints. This work advances non-equilibrium statistical mechanics by providing necessary conditions for steady-state homogeneity.
main_problem: To develop a general method determining when diffusion necessarily equilibrates in non-ideal reaction-diffusion (RD) systems driven by autonomous chemostats.
main_result: Diffusion equilibration is proven for RD systems whose underlying Chemical Reaction Network (CRN) is either pseudo-detailed balanced or complex balanced, provided specific constraints on the reaction fluxes are met.
method: The method constructs a kinetic potential acting as a Lyapunov function to analyze the time evolution of system free energy and entropy production rates.
model_or_system: Open, non-ideal RD systems in solution at constant T and V, governed by deterministic equations incorporating diffusion, chemical reactions, and external chemostat exchange. The analysis heavily utilizes Chemical Reaction Network (CRN) theory.
key_observables: Entropy production rates ($\sum_{	ext{rct}} [\mathbf{c}]$ and $\sum_{	ext{diff}} [\mathbf{c}]$), the kinetic potential ($\hat{F}[\mathbf{c}]$), and the chemical work rate ($\mathcal{W}_{	ext{chm}}$).
important_parameters: Temperature (T), volume (V), and the stoichiometric properties of the reaction network.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the macroscopic limit. Initial assumptions regarding chemostatted species being ideal are relaxed throughout the work.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates a pseudo-detailed balanced CRN, while Figure 2 illustrates a complex balanced CRN, relating network cycles to chemical graph loops.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by detailing the basic setup (Section II), introducing topological classifications of CRNs (Section III), deriving the main results based on these classes (Section IV), and concluding with discussions and comparisons (Section V).
why_interesting: While focused on classical non-equilibrium thermodynamics, the rigorous mathematical framework involving Lyapunov functions and detailed balance conditions is highly relevant to understanding steady states in open quantum systems or complex chemical dynamics.
